title: Isandro and the Cover
premise: Mirabel Thackeray, a crash investigator haunted by the deaths of her family in row twelve, receives a calendar invitation from a handler she knows is dead — and when she opens it, she is pulled into the meeting itself, waking inside a covert extraction operation. The team believes she was summoned as an asset; in truth, the dead handler arranged it, because Mirabel is the only person who can identify the forged flight manifest that doomed row twelve — and the defector they must extract before dawn is the forger. As the night unravels into betrayal, Mirabel discovers the defector is both bait and witness: the agency that killed her family wants him silenced on foreign soil. In the end, Mirabel chooses justice outside the law, trading her evidence to force the truth into daylight, letting the defector go free, and finally sleeping through the night.
about_author: Jonah Underhill is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reconstructing accident timelines before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about ordinary professionals trapped inside extraordinary conspiracies, drawing on his obsession with paper trails and the people they bury.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Two years after the crash, Mirabel works nights reconstructing other people's disasters, unable to sleep past 3:14 a.m. — the moment of impact. A routine audit of the old flight file reveals a manifest anomaly she once dismissed. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Her phone chimes: a calendar invite from Elias Vann, her former mentor, dead eleven months. Location: Hangar 9, tomorrow, 11 p.m. She reports it to no one and goes anyway, packing her crash-kit like a talisman. Emotional beat: dread braided with desperate hope.

chapters.title: Hangar Nine
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Inside the hangar, a four-person extraction team mistakes her for their new intelligence asset, 'Thackeray.' Before she can correct them, gunfire erupts — someone expected the meeting too. Emotional beat: vertigo of being mistaken for someone else.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: Team leader Okafor's POV. The team's objective surfaces: extract Anton Reyes, a documents forger hiding in the city, out on a dawn flight. Okafor suspects 'Thackeray' is not who the file says but needs her skills. Emotional beat: pragmatic distrust.

chapters.title: What the Manifest Said
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Shown a copy of the doomed flight's paperwork, Mirabel recognizes Reyes's forgery style instantly — he altered the manifest that put her family in row twelve. She conceals this and volunteers. Emotional beat: cold fury wearing a professional mask.

chapters.title: Dead Handler's Hand
chapters.summary: Interlude, Vann's POV via recovered notes. Flashback fragments reveal Vann discovered the forged manifest, faked his death, and scheduled the meeting to place Mirabel beside the one man who could name his killer. Emotional beat: posthumous guilt and calculation.

chapters.title: City of Locked Doors
chapters.summary: Mirabel and fixer Dane infiltrate Reyes's safehouse district. They find the safehouse burned two days ago — someone got there first. A neighbor's doorbell camera shows Reyes alive, fleeing. Emotional beat: the hunt tightening, hope curdling.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor briefs the team: intel suggests Reyes may be bait, dangled to draw out whoever killed Vann. He orders the mission continue anyway. Mirabel realizes the team might be expendable — including her. Emotional beat: loyalty under interrogation.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Following the camera trail, Mirabel corners Reyes in a laundromat basement. He doesn't run; he says her name and the seat numbers — 12A, 12B, 12C. Emotional beat: the collision of hunter and ghost.

chapters.title: Twelve A, B, C
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes confesses he forged the manifest under coercion from someone inside the agency — code name COVER — and kept proof as insurance. He never knew which passengers it condemned until he read the casualty list. Emotional beat: shame seeking absolution.

chapters.title: Insurance Policy
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Reyes's proof is a dead-drop key requiring a passphrase only Vann knew. Mirabel realizes Vann's invitation itself is the message — the meeting time matches the crash minute. Emotional beat: the dead speaking in timetables.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Dane's POV. En route to the drop, the team spots surveillance — COVER's cleaners have found them. A running chase through freight yards; Dane takes a graze wound covering Mirabel. Emotional beat: the team becoming a family under fire.

chapters.title: The Drop
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the dead-drop, the key opens a locker containing Vann's full dossier — naming COVER as Deputy Director Sarel Kess. Also inside: a photo proving Kess ordered Vann's death. Alarms trip; the locker was wired. Emotional beat: triumph ambushed.

chapters.title: Cleaners
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Ambushed at the rail yard, the team scatters. Okafor covers the retreat and is captured buying the others time, radioing one word: 'Fly.' Emotional beat: sacrifice without ceremony.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV, captive. Kess personally interrogates Okafor, revealing the plan: let the extraction proceed, then destroy the plane with Reyes aboard — another row-twelve-style 'accident' erasing the witness. Emotional beat: horror recognizing history repeating.

chapters.title: Dawn Is a Deadline
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. With two hours to wheels-up, Mirabel must choose: flee with the dossier or fly the extraction knowing the plane is the trap. She decides to board — to beat Kess at his own genre, the staged disaster. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Pre-Flight
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes and Mirabel board the charter as 'cleaners' close on the airfield. Mirabel, using her investigator's eye, finds the explosive charge rigged near the rear rows — rows twelve through fourteen. Emotional beat: expertise as weapon.

chapters.title: Kess's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. Kess monitors the airfield, confident the mathematics of plausible deniability will hold — until Mirabel transmits the dossier to forty newsrooms simultaneously mid-taxi. Emotional beat: control slipping through gloved fingers.

chapters.title: Climb-Out
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The charge detonates late and wrong — Mirabel had rerouted its trigger — punching a hole aft of row eleven. The damaged charter limps back onto the runway as cleaners storm the tarmac into arriving federal agents tipped by the broadcast. Emotional beat: survival as defiance.

chapters.title: COVER Torn Off
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, rapid cuts. Kess arrested on the tarmac; Okafor found alive in a holding cell; the dossier's manifest evidence formally reopens the crash investigation. Reyes surrenders willingly, choosing testimony over flight. Emotional beat: justice arriving by daylight.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Months later, Mirabel testifies at the hearing, reading the names of row twelve into the record. Reyes, sentenced but alive, meets her eyes across the chamber — neither forgiveness nor hatred, just acknowledgment. Emotional beat: grief given a public shape.

chapters.title: Sleeping Through the Night
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Back home, Mirabel files her final report, keeps Vann's battered watch running on her desk, and turns off the 3:14 a.m. alarm she no longer needs. She sleeps until morning. Emotional beat: belonging to the living again.
